portName: Roseau Cruise Ship Berth (Bayfront) and Woodbridge Bay Port
seoTitle: Roseau cruise port guide: Dominica berths, falls, reefs
seoDescription: Roseau's cruise berth is on the Bayfront, 5 min walk from the Old Market; Woodbridge Bay is about 1 km north. Trafalgar Falls is 25–30 min by taxi.
quickAnswer: Most ships dock at the Roseau Cruise Ship Berth on the Bayfront, about 5 minutes' walk from the Old Market and the museum; larger ships use Woodbridge Bay Port, about 1 km north, a 10–15 minute walk along Dame Eugenia Charles Boulevard. Trafalgar Falls and Champagne Reef need a taxi or tour, and taxi fares are agreed with the driver. Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard from town, and leave the falls or the reef 90 minutes before.
intro: Roseau is Dominica's small, busy capital, squeezed between the sea and steep green hills. The main cruise berth is right on the Bayfront, so you step off into town. Dominica's appeal is its rainforest and volcanic landscape rather than its beaches: Trafalgar Falls is about half an hour inland, the bubbling Champagne Reef is a short drive south, and the Botanic Gardens and Morne Bruce viewpoint are within walking distance. Most national park sites need a site pass, which you buy on site, not online. Roads are narrow and afternoon traffic in Roseau is slow, so build in time to get back.
tenderNotes: Large ships dock. Small expedition ships sometimes tender into Roseau.

terminals.name: Roseau Cruise Ship Berth (Bayfront)
terminals.notes: On the Bayfront in downtown Roseau, opposite the Old Market and the tourism office. Souvenir stalls are just past the gangway, and taxis, minibuses and tour buses wait at the berth. It takes one ship at a time.

terminals.name: Woodbridge Bay Port
terminals.notes: Deep-water port on the northern edge of Roseau, used when the town berth is taken and by the largest ships; the government says it is the island's only port with two gangways. About 10–15 minutes' walk into town along Dame Eugenia Charles Boulevard. Confirm where tour operators will collect you.

walkability.detail: From the Bayfront berth, the Old Market, the Dominica Museum and the shops are about 5 minutes' walk, and the Botanic Gardens about 15 minutes. Morne Bruce viewpoint is a further 20–30 minutes uphill from the gardens. From Woodbridge Bay add 10–15 minutes each way. Trafalgar Falls, Champagne Reef and Emerald Pool are not walkable.

transportSections.time: 5 min to the Old Market; 15 min to the Botanic Gardens
transportSections.detail: Pavements in central Roseau are narrow and busy. From Woodbridge Bay, walk south along Dame Eugenia Charles Boulevard, 10–15 minutes.

transportSections.cost: Agree the fare with the driver before you set off
transportSections.time: 10–15 min to Champagne Reef; 25–30 min to Trafalgar Falls; 40–45 min to Emerald Pool
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait at the cruise berth. Licensed taxis have number plates starting H, HA or HB; the US State Department advises using only clearly marked official taxis. No official fare list for cruise passengers was found, so agree the price, whether it is per person or per vehicle, the currency and the return time before you get in.

transportSections.cost: Low, standardised fares set by the government
transportSections.detail: Shared minibuses run from stops around Roseau during the day, but routes and times are not obvious to visitors and they are not suited to night travel. Use them only for trips where a delay will not threaten your return.

transportSections.cost: Varies; plus a local temporary driving licence
transportSections.detail: Drive on the left. You need a local temporary licence, available from rental offices or the Traffic Department in Roseau; the tourist board gives the age limits as 25–65 with two years' driving experience. Roads are often narrow, steep and potholed, so most cruise passengers are better off with a taxi or tour.

returnTiming.rule: Be on board 60 minutes before all-aboard from downtown Roseau (add 15 minutes if the ship is at Woodbridge Bay). Leave Trafalgar Falls, Champagne Reef or Mero Beach 90 minutes before all-aboard, and Emerald Pool 2 hours before.
returnTiming.detail: Afternoon traffic in Roseau is slow and the inland roads are narrow and winding, so the drive back can take longer than the drive out. Agree the return time with your driver when you are dropped off, and do not go to the falls after heavy rain.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Ask your driver or a vendor to call a taxi; Roseau is 10–15 minutes from Champagne Reef and about 30 minutes from Trafalgar Falls. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme at once.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Taxi (agree the fare) plus a site pass bought at the reception centre
diyVsExcursion.saving: Depends on the excursion price and the taxi fare you agree

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner

excursionAdvice: Roseau, the Botanic Gardens and Morne Bruce need no tour. A ship excursion is worth it for whale watching, for diving, and for longer inland trips such as Emerald Pool or the Kalinago Territory (about an hour each way), where the slow roads make a guaranteed return valuable. For Trafalgar Falls or Champagne Reef, a taxi with an agreed fare and return time works well if you start early.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 at the Bayfront berth and all-aboard is 17:30. Departure times vary by ship, so check your own all-aboard time and move the plan earlier if needed. At Woodbridge Bay, add 15 minutes each way for the walk.

steps.what: Walk off onto the Bayfront and look round the Old Market.
Taxi to Trafalgar Falls, about 25–30 minutes. Agree the fare and a pick-up time first.
Buy a site pass at the reception centre and walk 10–15 minutes to the viewing platform.
Walk to the Botanic Gardens, about 15 minutes, then climb to Morne Bruce for the view over the town.
Lunch in Roseau; browse Roseau Market Plaza or the Old Market for coffee, spices and fruit.
Taxi south to Champagne Reef, 10–15 minutes, and snorkel among the bubbles.
Taxi back to the Bayfront, 90 minutes before all-aboard.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Trafalgar Falls
sights.why: Twin waterfalls, about 125 ft and 75 ft high, in Morne Trois Pitons National Park, seen from a viewing platform.
sights.cost: Site pass required, bought at the reception centre; taxi extra
sights.tip: The walk to the platform is about 10–15 minutes. Do not go after heavy rain, wear shoes with grip, and do not try the boulder scramble to the base alone.

sights.name: Champagne Reef
sights.why: Snorkelling site in the Soufrière Scotts Head Marine Reserve, named after the bubbles from volcanic springs on the sea floor.
sights.cost: Taxi extra; check any charges on site
sights.tip: About 7 km south of Roseau, 10–15 minutes by taxi. Bring your own mask if you have one.

sights.name: Roseau Botanic Gardens
sights.why: 40-acre gardens opened in 1889, the largest green space in Roseau and home to Sisserou parrots, Dominica's national bird.
sights.cost: No fee listed by the tourist board
sights.tip: About 15 minutes' walk from the Bayfront berth. Combine with Morne Bruce.

sights.name: Morne Bruce viewpoint
sights.why: Hilltop view over Roseau, the harbour and your ship.
sights.tip: A fairly steep 20–30 minute walk up from the Botanic Gardens; bring water. You can also go by car.

sights.name: Dominica Museum and the Old Market
sights.why: Small museum in a former post office built in 1810, facing the Old Market, the site of colonial-era slave trading and now a market selling local produce.

sights.name: Emerald Pool
sights.why: Rainforest pool where a waterfall drops about 50 ft; a swim is possible.
sights.cost: Site pass required; taxi or tour extra
sights.tip: About 40–45 minutes from the port. Go with a tour or a driver who will wait, and leave 2 hours before all-aboard.

sights.name: Titou Gorge and Wotten Waven
sights.why: Narrow gorge in Wotten Waven, the village known for its hot springs.
sights.cost: Taxi extra; check charges on site
sights.tip: About 10 minutes from Trafalgar Falls, so the two pair well; do not try to add many more sites in one day.

beaches.name: Champagne Reef
beaches.note: Better for snorkelling than for sunbathing.

beaches.name: Mero Beach
beaches.note: Beach on the west coast with InDee's beach bar. Busiest on Sundays, when local families hold barbecues.

commonMistakes.mistake: Getting in a taxi without agreeing the fare.
commonMistakes.fix: No official cruise fare list is published. Agree the price, per person or per vehicle, the currency and the return time before you set off.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting to buy the national park site pass online or by card.
commonMistakes.fix: Passes cannot be bought online. Buy one at the site reception centre (Trafalgar Falls, Emerald Pool, Indian River) and carry cash.
Roads are narrow and winding and afternoon traffic in Roseau is slow. Leave the falls and the reef 90 minutes before all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Visiting the waterfalls after heavy rain.
commonMistakes.fix: Rivers rise quickly and rocks get slippery. Choose Champagne Reef or the Botanic Gardens instead on a wet morning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting which berth the ship is at.
commonMistakes.fix: If the ship is at Woodbridge Bay, about 1 km north, tell your driver and allow 10–15 minutes more on foot.

safety: The US State Department rates Dominica Level 1, exercise normal precautions (May 2026), and the UK FCDO says the crime rate is low. Theft and vehicle break-ins do happen, so do not leave valuables unattended and avoid walking alone on empty streets or isolated beaches after dark. Use only clearly marked official taxis. Sea currents can be stronger than they look and not all beaches have lifeguards. Roads are often narrow and in poor condition. Hurricane season runs from June to November. Tap water is generally safe to drink, and ambulance cover is limited, so a taxi to hospital may be faster after an injury.
scams: Unofficial taxis: the US State Department advises using only clearly marked official taxis; licensed ones have H, HA or HB number plates.
Taxi fares disputed at the end of the trip: agree the price, per person or per vehicle, and the currency before you set off.
accessibility: The Bayfront berth puts you straight into flat downtown streets, but pavements are narrow and busy and the Botanic Gardens and Morne Bruce involve slopes. Trafalgar Falls has a short walk to the viewing platform, and most other nature sites involve rough or wet paths. Woodbridge Bay adds a 1 km walk or a taxi ride into town. Book a suitable vehicle in advance if you use a wheelchair.
rainyDay: Rain is common in the interior. Stay in Roseau for the Dominica Museum, the Old Market and the Market Plaza, or snorkel at Champagne Reef, and skip the waterfalls after heavy rain, when rivers run high.
crowdTips: On days with more than one ship, larger ships use Woodbridge Bay and the popular sites such as Trafalgar Falls fill as tour groups arrive. Start early, go to the falls first, and leave Roseau's sights for the afternoon. Mero Beach is busiest on Sundays.

faqs.a: No for most ships. They dock at the Roseau Cruise Ship Berth on the Bayfront or at Woodbridge Bay Port. Some small expedition ships tender.

faqs.q: Is Roseau walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes from the Bayfront berth: the Old Market is about 5 minutes away and the Botanic Gardens about 15. From Woodbridge Bay it is a 10–15 minute walk into town.

faqs.q: How do I get from Roseau cruise port to Trafalgar Falls?
faqs.a: By taxi or tour, about 25–30 minutes each way. Agree the fare and pick-up time first, and buy a site pass at the reception centre.

faqs.q: What can I do in Roseau in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Trafalgar Falls in the morning, the Botanic Gardens and Morne Bruce at midday, and snorkelling at Champagne Reef in the afternoon.
Champagne Reef, 10–15 minutes south by taxi, is the best for snorkelling. Mero Beach is 20–30 minutes north. There is no beach within walking distance of the berth.

faqs.q: Do I need a site pass in Dominica?
faqs.a: Yes for national park sites such as Trafalgar Falls and Emerald Pool. Buy it on site; passes cannot be bought online.

faqs.q: Is Roseau safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Generally yes. The US rates Dominica Level 1 and the UK says crime is low. Take normal care with valuables and use marked official taxis.

faqs.q: What currency is used in Dominica?
faqs.a: The Eastern Caribbean dollar (EC$). Carry cash, as cards may carry a fee and ATMs are sometimes out of order.
